content.text:
Current internal scene model:
- View A: attention is almost entirely on the lower location (selection probability 0.99968). The model represents that lower as very likely green and cross-shaped (recoverability now 0.629; after one step 0.459; after two 0.336). Other A locations are weakly represented: left is likely yellow circle, upper a blue square, right a red triangle (each with very low selection probability and lower recoverability).
- View B: attention is almost entirely on the left location (selection probability 0.99994). That left item is represented as yellow and cross-shaped (recoverability now 0.451; one step 0.333; two 0.253). B also contains a red circle at lower, a blue square at right, and a green triangle at upper with low current selection probabilities and modest recoverability.

How redirection would change selection (per the model):
- In View A, commanding “upper”, “right”, “lower” or “left” strongly drives selection to the corresponding location (each command yields ~0.999 probability of the named location), so the system can reliably reallocate attention within A.
- In View B, the left location is currently dominant; however the model’s command mappings indicate the upper location would be selected with high probability under many commands (so some commands would shift selection to upper), while other B locations remain unlikely to be chosen by commands.
